records.deidentified_narrative: ofc. keen1787ir#: 21-505090video: yes on march 27th, 2021, i was patrolling south side beat 53 police responded to home depot located at 2410 s georgia in reference to a pedestrian vs vehicle. upon arrival i made contact with the driver who was identified as campbell, cory [w/m, dob:[date], dl#:225525930, address: 1881 n 840 w] cory advised me he was driving west bound in the parking lot attempting to find a parking spot when a guy came and picked a kid from in front of his truck. he did not realize he had hit anything until this time. cory vehicle was identified as a black 2007 chevrolet silverado [ utah plate: f54-2jp, vin: 3gcek13m67g531522] cody vehicle did have any damage to it. as i made contact with the victims father identified as patel, rames [w/m, address: 800 w 2nd, phone: (580)630-2969] rames advised me that he was coming out of home depot as his kids were loading into the car with his wife, when the victim seen him coming out of home depot he then ran across the parking lot to go to him. as the victim was running towards him, he ran in front of the suspect vehicle. rames advised he thinks the right tire of the suspect vehicle hit the victims right foot. he identified the victim as patel, rihan [w/m, dob:[date]] rihan did have apparent minor injury to is right foot. at this time, ams did arrive on scene and transport rihan to bsa per request of his family. both parties where given the ir number for reference. i have nothing further to report. ofc. keen1787, 23:35, [date]

records.deidentified_narrative: on march 16, 2021 at approximately 2225 hours, i deputy mccellon 14448, was dispatched to 19950 fm 1485; 1485 bar in reference to a motor vehicle accident that occurred in the parking lot of the establishment. the reportee advised dispatch that his fiance, tasha hietbrink, was standing in the parking lot talking to someone when a female driver, kay torrey unit 1, backed into his fiance, pinning his fiance between the actor vehicle and another vehicle, unit 2. the victim was able to free herself from being pinned, and the reportee advised dispatch that she was conscious and breathing. medic 30 and east montgomery county fire made scene before my arrival at 2229 hours. in the process of the event, unit 2 received damage to its rear passenger side door. the driver in unit 2 was not injured. upon my arrival at approximately 2245, there firefighters on scene advised me that the female victim, identified as tasha hietbrink, was already onboard the ambulance and [medical facility]. tasha complained of lower body pain as a result of the incident. medic 30 transported [medical facility]. numerous people on scene then pointed towards inside the bar. they identified an older white female as the driver of the actor vehicle. i went inside the establishment and made contact with the female who agreed to come outside to be interviewed. the female identified herself a kay torrey dob [date]. during questioning kay admitted to getting into the vehicle to leave the bar. she stated that she was backing up out of her parking spot, and suddenly felt the car stop like she hit something. she stated that she then heard people screaming, and then another person ran up to her driver’s side window and told her that she had just hit someone. kay denies trying to leave the scene. kay advised that she was not injured during the incident. during my interview, i noticed that kay smelled very strongly of alcohol. kay slurred her words and swayed on her feet throughout our entire interaction. kay admitted to having ""a few"" drinks tonight, but then later stated that she only had two vodka-cranberry drinks. the bartender employed by 1485 bar and several patrons advised me that kay had been ""cut off"" by the bartender at approximately 1930 hours due to the bartender's perception of kay's intoxication levels. we relocated to an adjacent gas station parking lot that provided adequate lighting and a flat surface to perform standardized field sobriety tests (sfsts). i am certified to conduct sfsts including horizontal gaze nystagmus. i administered the horizontal gaze nystagmus test to kay torrey. kay was able to maintain her balance and the correct positioning during the instruction phase and throughout the performance of the test. i checked kay's eyes for equal pupil size and equal tracking. i observed nystagmus during the lack of smooth pursuit portion of the hgn test, accounting for 2 of 6 hgn clues. i observed nystagmus during the distinct and sustained nystagmus at maximum deviation portion of the hgn test, accounting for 4 of 6 hgn clues. i observed nystagmus during the onset of nystagmus prior to 45 degrees portion of the hgn test, accounting for 6 of 6 hgn clues. i determined that due to kay's lack of balance in addition to her injury, it was not safe for kay to attempt the walk and turn, nor the one leg stand test. kay torrey was placed into custody for dwi/dui.

records.public_safe_text: on march 16, 2021 at approximately 2225 hours, i deputy mccellon 14448, was dispatched to 19950 fm 1485; 1485 bar in reference to a motor vehicle accident that occurred in the parking lot of the establishment. the reportee advised dispatch that his fiance, tasha hietbrink, was standing in the parking lot talking to someone when a female driver, kay torrey unit 1, backed into his fiance, pinning his fiance between the actor vehicle and another vehicle, unit 2. the victim was able to free herself from being pinned, and the reportee advised dispatch that she was conscious and breathing. medic 30 and east montgomery county fire made scene before my arrival at 2229 hours. in the process of the event, unit 2 received damage to its rear passenger side door. the driver in unit 2 was not injured. upon my arrival at approximately 2245, there firefighters on scene advised me that the female victim, identified as tasha hietbrink, was already onboard the ambulance and [medical facility]. tasha complained of lower body pain as a result of the incident. medic 30 transported [medical facility]. numerous people on scene then pointed towards inside the bar. they identified an older white female as the driver of the actor vehicle. i went inside the establishment and made contact with the female who agreed to come outside to be interviewed. the female identified herself a kay torrey dob [date]. during questioning kay admitted to getting into the vehicle to leave the bar. she stated that she was backing up out of her parking spot, and suddenly felt the car stop like she hit something. she stated that she then heard people screaming, and then another person ran up to her driver’s side window and told her that she had just hit someone. kay denies trying to leave the scene. kay advised that she was not injured during the incident. during my interview, i noticed that kay smelled very strongly of alcohol. kay slurred her words and swayed on her feet throughout our entire interaction. kay admitted to having ""a few"" drinks tonight, but then later stated that she only had two vodka-cranberry drinks. the bartender employed by 1485 bar and several patrons advised me that kay had been ""cut off"" by the bartender at approximately 1930 hours due to the bartender's perception of kay's intoxication levels. we relocated to an adjacent gas station parking lot that provided adequate lighting and a flat surface to perform standardized field sobriety tests (sfsts). i am certified to conduct sfsts including horizontal gaze nystagmus. i administered the horizontal gaze nystagmus test to kay torrey. kay was able to maintain her balance and the correct positioning during the instruction phase and throughout the performance of the test. i checked kay's eyes for equal pupil size and equal tracking. i observed nystagmus during the lack of smooth pursuit portion of the hgn test, accounting for 2 of 6 hgn clues. i observed nystagmus during the distinct and sustained nystagmus at maximum deviation portion of the hgn test, accounting for 4 of 6 hgn clues. i observed nystagmus during the onset of nystagmus prior to 45 degrees portion of the hgn test, accounting for 6 of 6 hgn clues. i determined that due to kay's lack of balance in addition to her injury, it was not safe for kay to attempt the walk and turn, nor the one leg stand test. kay torrey was placed into custody for dwi/dui.

records.public_safe_text: while on patrol police responded to the above listed address for a major accident involving a pedestrian. details to the call stated the pedestrian (unit 2) had been run over two times by a vehicle that was reversing. when i arrived on scene i located unit 2 who was already being seen by ems. unit 2 did not have life threatening injuries. unit 2 stated she was walking behind a car (unit 1) that was parked in a parking spot. unit 2 stated she thought the driver of the unit 1 saw her, but unit 1 reversed and bumped into unit 2, knocking unit 2 to the floor. unit 2 stated she wasn't sure if she was run over by unit 1 or not but unit 2 did have a swollen right foot. based off of unit 2's injuries i suspected unit 1 ran over unit 2's foot. unit 2 stated unit 1 then left the scene without stopping to render aid (reference mark 43 report for offence report). unit 2 was not able to get a good description of unit 1. unit 2 stated all she knows is that unit 1 was a black and red car. i contacted tid detective who advised me that since their was no debris left at the scene, a csi would not be necessary. unit 2 was handed a case card and was transported to the address listed above for her minor injuries. dmea

records.deidentified_narrative: unit#1 was [roadway]. and turning right on red. unit#1 stated she stopped looked both ways and was looking left as she pulled out to make sure it was clear. unit#1's driver was making her turn then saw that (ped1) and (ped2) were in front of her car and slammed on the brakes. unit#1's driver didn't believe she made contact with (ped2) but (ped1) stated she did.(ped1) stated she was [roadway]. (ped1) stated she started to cross while the crosswalk signal was flashing red. (ped1) stated she was holding (ped2)'s hand and he was on her left.(ped2) was asked what happened and would only repeat he got hit in his back and kept pointing between his upper back/shoulder blades. when i asked a question requiring an different answer, (ped2) kept looking back to family as if he didn't know what to say and wanted them to tell him what to say. i moved (ped2) over by the car to show me what part of the car made contact with him. (ped2) pointed to the front left head light. i had (ped2) stand next to the car and noted the bumper stuck out further than the headlights and (ped2) should have made contact on his butt/lower back. (ped2) then leaned back along the car to make it so the headlight would hit his upper back. i asked (ped2) how he ended up like that, i asked if he flopped back on the car when it came close to him and he stated no his mother yanked his arm and he bent back and hit the car.(w1)-amazon driver stated that he was driving by at 45mph hour and saw unit#1 do a rolling stop and then clip (ped2). (w1) stated that he stopped and gave (ped1) his information and left before pd arrived.(w2)-passenger in vehicle that was stopped on the opposite side of the intersection facing toward unit#1. (w2) stated that unit#1 stopped and began her turn and then (ped1) walked out in front of her with (ped2). (w2) stated that (unit#1) stopped before contact was made and that (ped1) was making up that (ped2) got tapped by the car. due to the conflicting stories it was hard to say if contact had actually been made. (ped1) lifted the shirt and showed me (ped2)'s back and there was no marks, bruising or redness noted. there was no marks/damage noted on unit#1. i explained to (ped1) and unit#1's driver what was said by all parties and the problems with the versions of each in deciding if (ped2) made contact with unit#1 and if it did happen was it unit#1's fault or (ped1)'s fault for yanking him. also noted was that (ped2) would have been perpendicular to unit#1 and should not have been hit on the back but [roadway] for that to have happened is for him to have been turned rapidly. it is possible that (ped1) pulled/yanked (ped2) because she though unit#1 was going to hit them and this turned (ped2) to his back facing unit#1. unknown if unit#1 then struck (ped2) or (ped2) was yanked onto the car by (ped1).(ped1) stated that she wasn't planning on filing anything just didn't want people thinking she made up the store for money like (w2) allegedly accused her off. (ped1) did not indicate she was going to take (ped2) to get checked out for anything.

records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to the listed location for a major crash. officers arrived before me and attended to all parties. when we arrived unit 1 was stuck inside the north side of the listed location. an individual was inside the location at the time of the collision. the individual suffered some injuries and was being treated by ems when i arrived. ems informed us that the individual may have a broken [medical facility] for medical treatment. i spoke with the driver of unit 1 and did not observe any apparent signs of intoxication on the driver. the driver did not have slurred speech or an odor of alcohol coming from her. i conducted the horizontal gaze nystagmus test on the driver but did not see any clues. the driver stated that she had just arrived at the store to get gas but she noticed that the pumps were not working so she attempted to park in front of the store. the driver stated that she was very sure that she pushed on the brake but when she did the vehicle accelerated. i asked her multiple times if it was possible that she mistakenly pushed the accelerator instead. the driver insisted that she pushed the brake. i spoke with the passengers in the vehicle and they both stated that there was not anything that could have distracted the driver and caused her to push the accelerator. they both believe that the vehicle had a mechanical fault. the store manager arrived and allowed me to see the security footage of the incident. i watched it and observed that uni1 arrived to the location and went to park. unit 1 appeared to be parking when it continued through the front of the store instead. it appeared to me that the driver of unit 1 mistakenly pushed the gas pedal accelerating into the front of the store. this did not appear to be intentional. we called our traffic investigations unit and informed them of the situation. i gave the [case id] to the store manager for her reference. dme

records.deidentified_narrative: on april 17th, 2021 at approximately 2152 hours officer c. arredondo #244 with the anthony texas police department received a call, via cell phone, from sgt. a. martinez #32, of the anthony new mexico police department, reference a motor vehicle accident involving a marked anthony new mexico police unit and an unknown male pedestrian. the accident had occurred in the pilot travel center parking lot located at [roadway]. in anthony, el paso county, texas. the pilot travel center parking lot is a paved, publicly accessible private parking lot. officer arredondo arrived at address of occurrence and made contact with sgt. martinez. sgt. martinez, the driver of unit 1, stated he exited the pilot travel center and entered his vehicle, a marked anthony new mexico police unit # a-10, bearing new mexico registration [identifier], which was parked in front of the business. the driver of unit 1 further stated that, upon exiting the pilot travel center, he observed an elderly male closely follow him out of the establishment and follow him toward unit 1. the driver of unit 1 stated he then entered his vehicle and looked in all directions, in order to safely back out of the parking slot. he then stated that he put unit 1 in reverse, started to back up, and came to a complete, abrupt, stop when he heard a faint thud from the back of unit 1. the driver of unit 1 stated he exited the vehicle and observed a male pedestrian on the pavement directly behind unit 1. the driver of unit 1 stated that he immediately rendered aid and asked the male pedestrian if he was in need of medical attention which the male pedestrian declined. the driver of unit 1 stated that he made several attempts to get medical attention for the male pedestrian, however the male pedestrian continued to decline and stated that he just wanted to leave. the driver of unit 1 stated that several bystanders rushed to the elderly male with phones in hand recording the incident, but none of them stayed at the scene to give statements or witness accounts to responding officers. the driver of unit 1 stated that he, and the bystanders, assisted the male pedestrian to his feet. shortly after he was on his feet however, the male pedestrian walked away from the driver of unit 1 and boarded a bus that was parked on the east end of the parking lot, failing to provide identifying information or remain at the scene to provide any statement to responding authorities. officer arredondo obtained video surveillance footage from the buildings east corner camera. based on video surveillance footage, both the driver of unit 1, and the male pedestrian, wearing dark clothing, exit the business at approximately the same time. as the driver of unit 1 opens the vehicle door, the male pedestrian inches toward the passenger side blind spot of unit 1. as the driver of unit 1 enters the vehicle, the male pedestrian walks directly behind unit 1. unit 1 is then shifted into reverse, initiating the vehicles red brake lights as well as white back-up lights before backing. it is observed that, as the lights are illuminated, the male pedestrian continues walking directly behind the vehicle, toward the east end of the parking lot, and is struck by unit 1. throughout the entire incident, the male pedestrian appears to have an unknown object in his right hand and appears to be looking down at the unknown object as he is walking. as unit 1 strikes the male pedestrian, the driver of unit 1 immediately stops and exits the vehicle to render aid to the male pedestrian. as the driver of unit 1 is assisting the male pedestrian, five unknown bystanders approach the driver of unit 1, and the male pedestrian, crowding around the male pedestrian as he is on the pavement, eventually assisting him to his feet. the pedestrian then walks away, toward the east end of the parking lot, out of the surveillance camera frame. none of the witnesses or bystanders, observed on surveillance footage, stayed to provide any information to the responding officers. officer arredondo was later notified, by pilot travel center staff, that the bus which the male pedestrian entered, belonged to bus company viajes aztecas. an employee from a separate viajes aztecas bus, cordero, jesus dob [date], came forward and contacted the staff that was on the bus the male pedestrian had boarded via cell phone. officer arredondo, via cell phone, spoke with garcia, mario dob [date], who is a bus attendant on the bus which the male pedestrian boarded. garcia handed the phone to a male who was reportedly the pedestrian involved the incident. officer arredondo spoke with an unverified male who stated his name was miramontes, javier [date] and stated he was the male pedestrian involved in the motor vehicle accident. miramontes stated that he did not stand by and left the scene of the accident because he was on vacation he could not stay behind. miramontes stated that he was walking behind unit 1 when he was struck. miramontes stated he sustained injuries to the left side of his face, left knee and also broke his glasses when he fell to the pavement. officer arredondo advised miramontes that he would need to provide an in-person statement in order to assist in the investigation of the motor vehicle accident. miramontes stated that it would be difficult to do so because he lives in los angeles, california. officer arredondo made several attempts to obtain contact information from miramontes, however miramontes stated that he would have his daughter contact officer arredondo via cell phone. officer arredondo was unable to verify if miramontes was in fact the pedestrian who was struck by unit 1. officer arredondo obtained surveillance footage and records.public_safe_text: on april 17th, 2021 at approximately 2152 hours officer c. arredondo #244 with the anthony texas police department received a call, via cell phone, from sgt. a. martinez #32, of the anthony new mexico police department, reference a motor vehicle accident involving a marked anthony new mexico police unit and an unknown male pedestrian. the accident had occurred in the pilot travel center parking lot located at [roadway]. in anthony, el paso county, texas. the pilot travel center parking lot is a paved, publicly accessible private parking lot. officer arredondo arrived at address of occurrence and made contact with sgt. martinez. sgt. martinez, the driver of unit 1, stated he exited the pilot travel center and entered his vehicle, a marked anthony new mexico police unit # a-10, bearing new mexico registration [identifier], which was parked in front of the business. the driver of unit 1 further stated that, upon exiting the pilot travel center, he observed an elderly male closely follow him out of the establishment and follow him toward unit 1. the driver of unit 1 stated he then entered his vehicle and looked in all directions, in order to safely back out of the parking slot. he then stated that he put unit 1 in reverse, started to back up, and came to a complete, abrupt, stop when he heard a faint thud from the back of unit 1. the driver of unit 1 stated he exited the vehicle and observed a male pedestrian on the pavement directly behind unit 1. the driver of unit 1 stated that he immediately rendered aid and asked the male pedestrian if he was in need of medical attention which the male pedestrian declined. the driver of unit 1 stated that he made several attempts to get medical attention for the male pedestrian, however the male pedestrian continued to decline and stated that he just wanted to leave. the driver of unit 1 stated that several bystanders rushed to the elderly male with phones in hand recording the incident, but none of them stayed at the scene to give statements or witness accounts to responding officers. the driver of unit 1 stated that he, and the bystanders, assisted the male pedestrian to his feet. shortly after he was on his feet however, the male pedestrian walked away from the driver of unit 1 and boarded a bus that was parked on the east end of the parking lot, failing to provide identifying information or remain at the scene to provide any statement to responding authorities. officer arredondo obtained video surveillance footage from the buildings east corner camera. based on video surveillance footage, both the driver of unit 1, and the male pedestrian, wearing dark clothing, exit the business at approximately the same time. as the driver of unit 1 opens the vehicle door, the male pedestrian inches toward the passenger side blind spot of unit 1. as the driver of unit 1 enters the vehicle, the male pedestrian walks directly behind unit 1. unit 1 is then shifted into reverse, initiating the vehicles red brake lights as well as white back-up lights before backing. it is observed that, as the lights are illuminated, the male pedestrian continues walking directly behind the vehicle, toward the east end of the parking lot, and is struck by unit 1. throughout the entire incident, the male pedestrian appears to have an unknown object in his right hand and appears to be looking down at the unknown object as he is walking. as unit 1 strikes the male pedestrian, the driver of unit 1 immediately stops and exits the vehicle to render aid to the male pedestrian. as the driver of unit 1 is assisting the male pedestrian, five unknown bystanders approach the driver of unit 1, and the male pedestrian, crowding around the male pedestrian as he is on the pavement, eventually assisting him to his feet. the pedestrian then walks away, toward the east end of the parking lot, out of the surveillance camera frame. none of the witnesses or bystanders, observed on surveillance footage, stayed to provide any information to the responding officers. officer arredondo was later notified, by pilot travel center staff, that the bus which the male pedestrian entered, belonged to bus company viajes aztecas. an employee from a separate viajes aztecas bus, cordero, jesus dob [date], came forward and contacted the staff that was on the bus the male pedestrian had boarded via cell phone. officer arredondo, via cell phone, spoke with garcia, mario dob [date], who is a bus attendant on the bus which the male pedestrian boarded. garcia handed the phone to a male who was reportedly the pedestrian involved the incident. officer arredondo spoke with an unverified male who stated his name was miramontes, javier [date] and stated he was the male pedestrian involved in the motor vehicle accident. miramontes stated that he did not stand by and left the scene of the accident because he was on vacation he could not stay behind. miramontes stated that he was walking behind unit 1 when he was struck. miramontes stated he sustained injuries to the left side of his face, left knee and also broke his glasses when he fell to the pavement. officer arredondo advised miramontes that he would need to provide an in-person statement in order to assist in the investigation of the motor vehicle accident. miramontes stated that it would be difficult to do so because he lives in los angeles, california. officer arredondo made several attempts to obtain contact information from miramontes, however miramontes stated that he would have his daughter contact officer arredondo via cell phone. officer arredondo was unable to verify if miramontes was in fact the pedestrian who was struck by unit 1. officer arredondo obtained surveillance footage and photo evidence of pilot travel center parking lot layout and unit 1. unit 1 did not appear to have sustained any damage and the area was canvased for any sign of injury sustained by the male pedestrian however none was found. this investigation is closed and complete upon receiving further testimony from the male pedestrian.
